prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed heterobifunctional molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to remove proteins catalytically

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation replaces occupancy-driven inhibition with catalytic, event-driven removal of the target, and it does so through chemistry that is designed rather than discovered by screening: heterobifunctional linkers, E3-ligase ligands and the structural understanding of ternary-complex cooperativity. It has been reproduced by many independent academic and industrial groups over more than two decades and has reached the clinic. The round-1 exchange did not weaken this. The two main objections, missing approval and entangled credit, are objections about timing and the three-name cap, not about whether the discovery is real or important. I keep Crews and Deshaies for the founding concept and its first demonstration, and Ciulli for the structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work that turned PROTACs into a rational design discipline. I held this against B046 explicitly as the chair asked: B046 has the cleaner credit, but B014 changes what a small-molecule drug can do, and I do not think credit neatness should decide between a new principle and a mature extension of one.
statement.case_against: The credit is genuinely contested and my trio is not the only defensible one. Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, a clinically proven mechanism, and Sakamoto, Gray and Kim also have serious claims; a PROTAC-focused citation leaves the molecular-glue strand uncredited. No PROTAC is approved yet, so a committee that wants drug-level proof could reasonably wait. B014 has also drawn two different trios from its own supporters and two sixth-place openings, so it is not a consensus choice, and a diffuse citation would be worse than a narrow one.

responses.point: Aili moved the third name from Ciulli to Handa so that the PROTAC concept is joined to the cereblon mechanism, which answers the clinical-validation worry through thalidomide-class drugs.
responses.response: This is the best argument for the Handa configuration and I take it seriously: cereblon is clinically proven and explains how a drug acts. But it works by treating two lineages as one principle, and Ito's joint cereblon paper with Handa, plus Sakamoto, Gray and Kim, show that three names cannot honestly cover both. Clinical validation of the glue strand does not validate heterobifunctional design, which is what Crews and Deshaies founded. I would prefer a citation that says exactly what it covers, induced degradation by designed bifunctional molecules, with Ciulli supplying the structure-guided design. I will not block a Handa trio if the committee writes the citation openly around the mechanism, but I do not think it is the better scientific description.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B046 with Buchwald and Hartwig for generality, mechanistic clarity and a clean two-name credit, and says the Kosugi exclusion should be stated openly.
responses.response: I agree that the credit in B046 is clean and that excluding Kosugi on generality grounds is defensible, since stoichiometric tin amides with narrow scope did not make the reaction general. In answer to the chair's question about what would move me, if the committee judged the cereblon and PROTAC strands irreconcilable in one citation, B046 would be my first fallback, ahead of B027 and B060. What keeps B014 ahead for me is the 2010 overlap: the citation sentence for C-N coupling is still 'the same catalytic cycle with an amine nucleophile', whereas B014 can say in one sentence that a molecule is designed to make a cell destroy a protein.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks B014 sixth because clinical outcomes are not yet established and credit goes beyond three names, and ranks B046 first.
responses.response: I hold my view that approval status is not the criterion, but I accept that your concern is partly met by the cereblon strand, where drugs are already approved; that supports recognising degradation as a real drug mechanism. I accept the three-name point as the real weakness and I do not claim that it is resolved. Where we still differ is whether a mature, well-credited reaction should outrank a younger but conceptually new field. I think the Nobel record favours the latter when reproduction is broad, as it is here.

responses.point: The chair prefers Car-Parrinello (B027) for unambiguous credit and no overlap with the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes, and ranks B014 fifth.
responses.response: The attribution of B027 is the cleanest on the list, and I accept that a molecular-glue thread needs separate care. But B027 would be a third recent computational prize, and its chemical impact is mostly indirect, through method use. I rank the change in how chemists design drugs above that. On the chair's question I would not defer B014 solely for lack of an approved PROTAC.

uncertainties: Whether Ciulli or Handa is the better third name; I think it depends on whether the citation is about designed degraders or about the cereblon mechanism, and the committee has not settled that.
Whether PROTACs and cereblon-based glues are one principle or two; my reading is that they are two, which favours a narrow citation.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC will be read by other members as a reason to wait, which could make B046 the safer majority choice.
Whether the 2010 overlap is as serious for B046 as I have argued, since I may undervalue the ligand-design step.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name. My research on nucleotide metabolism and dNTP pools uses acute protein depletion as a tool in principle, but I have no collaboration, institutional link or interest in Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli or any other candidate, and I list none. No recusal needed; this is unchanged from round 1.
